To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed PCL/Gel and PCL/Gel/Hyaluronic acid nanofiber scaffolding for GBM and that these scaffolds are promising for the study of the glioblastoma tumor and for the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
PCL/Gel/Hyaluronic acid composite scaffolds with random and aligned nanofibres were successfully fabricated by using electrospinning.
the incorporation of HA into the PCL/Geltan nanofibers can mimic the ECM of GBM and can be used as an in vitro model for studying GBM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biomimetic nanofibrous scaffolds for GBM.
the fabrication and characterization of electrospun PCL/Gel/HAscaffolds as a biomimicry matrix for glioblastoma.
developing a biomaterial scaffold that mimics the extracellular matrix for the study of glioblastoma tumor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrospun PCL/Gel/HAscaffolds can be used as a promising candidate for GBM tumor engineering.
the PCL/GEL/HA scaffolds are promising candidates for mimicking GBM extracellular matrix.
the PCL/GEL/HA composite nanofibers are promising scaffolds for the development of a novel tissue engineering strategy for GBM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully engineered PCL/Gel/Hyaluronic acid nanofiber scaffolding with aligned and random nanofibrous structures to mimic the extracellular matrix (GBM ECM) of glioblastoma tumor.

the nanofibrous structure of PCL/Gel and PCL/Gel/Gel/HA with aligned and random nanofibrous scaffolds could be considered as a suitable platform for mimicking the ECM of GBM tumor and for investigating the tumor behavior.
the electrospun nanoscaffolds can be designed to mimic GBM extracellular matrix for the study of tumor biology and for the development of new therapeutic strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PCL/Gel and PCL/Gel/GHA nanofibers can be used for mimicking the ECM of GBM and for the study of GBM tumor.
the incorporation of hyaluronic acids into the PCL/gelatin nanofibers improved the cell adhesion and axon growth, which may be useful for GBM treatment.
the nanofibers can be used for mimicking the GBM microenvironment and for the study of the behavior of glioma cells.
